newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia faces average summer rain - bureau.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia faces average summer rain - bureau.

text.p: Only relatively small areas of Australia were forecast to have summer (December-February) rainfall at above or below average, the Bureau of Meterorology said in a seasonal climate outlook statement on Tuesday.
There was a bias toward wetter than normal, particularly in the eastern states of Queensland and New South Wales, it said.

Isolated areas in Western Australia and South Australia had a significant chance of recording below average summer total rainfall, it said. Above and below average equate to rankings in the top or bottom 30 percent of totals, the bureau said.

Predictions are based on southern oscillation index (SOI) trends and recent rainfall patterns. The SOI for November was zero, the lowest value for the year and a drop of four points from October, the bureau said.
This continued the pattern of fairly netural SOI values experienced throughout the year, it said.
Ocean temperatures in the eastern Pacific Ocean continue to be slightly cooler than average, particularly at depth, it said.
Computer predictions of the central to eastern tropical Pacific sea surface temperature all indicate a persistence of conditions near normal for the remainder of summer, it said.
